title: Make admin a product bridge, not a configuration wall
summary: Filter Presets should bridge reusable backend behavior into Elementor-editable templates, while CPT management should prioritize a clear repeatable field builder with advanced WordPress registration options tucked away.
rationale: The previous operational reset removed the architecture-builder shell but still left confusing forms: presets exposed too many internal runtime knobs at once, and CPT meta fields were presented as a fixed set of rows. The product direction is closer to a simpler JetSmartFilters plus JetEngine: WordPress owns reusable data structures and Elementor owns visual/template editing. Therefore the admin should create useful WordPress contracts and hand the implementer into Elementor for layout and styling.
alternatives_considered: Keep all filter layout concerns inside the preset form
Build a custom filter visual builder inside the plugin admin
Expose every WordPress CPT registration argument at first glance
Remove the backend admin and leave everything inside Elementor widgets
evidence: User correction on 2026-05-18: the plugin should be a product-like, reusable JetSmartFilters/JetEngine alternative, but around 15 percent simpler and not a custom builder replacing Elementor.
Existing Simple Budget Plugin uses plugin-owned Elementor templates as an effective bridge: admin creates/discovers templates, Elementor edits visual structure, widgets consume selected contracts.
Current EIT Filter Controller already supports selecting admin presets from Elementor, so a template bridge can reuse existing runtime instead of inventing a new builder.
risks: Elementor template creation must validate Elementor availability, ownership metadata, capability, and delete permissions.
Repeatable CPT fields need a server-side cap even if the UI lets users add rows dynamically, otherwise option payloads can grow without a safety boundary.
The first bridge pass creates editable Elementor templates but does not implement full Theme Builder Pro registration.
